mainTopic: Why does רבי שמעון say a dangling limb or flesh is not treated as food? רבי זירא challenges the reason given in the name of רבי יוחנן, and רבי אסי explains which part of the משנה that reason refers to.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יוחנן's reason, quoted by רבי אסי, for רבי שמעון's view about flesh or a limb hanging from an animal: food that cannot be given to others to eat is not called food. רבי זירא suggests a simpler reason, that the hanging piece is still attached, and supports it with the case of a split fig branch. רבי אסי answers that the reason belongs to the middle case of the משנה, where the animal was slaughtered. רבי זירא objects that the middle case already has other explanations. So the גמרא settles on the last case, where the animal died, and applies רבי שמעון's ruling to the hanging flesh. A new משנה then deals with a limb or flesh hanging from a person, where רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון disagree after the person dies. The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון is speaking generally: he holds that a limb from a dead body is not טמא. It shows the same argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. It then finds the practical difference between a limb from the living and a limb from the dead, using a משנה about small pieces of flesh and bone that come off such a limb. The chapter הָעוֹר וְהָרוֹטֶב then ends.

steps.title: Food that others cannot eat is not called food
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of רבי יוחנן's explanation, quoted by רבי אסי, of רבי שמעון's view: food that cannot be given to others to eat does not count as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Food that you cannot feed] to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a statement that began just before this section. רבי אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains רבי שמעון's view: something no one at all may eat, not even others, is not considered אוכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something only counts as אוכל for the laws of טומאת אוכלין if it is food people may actually eat. A hanging limb or flesh is forbidden even to non-Jews as אבר מן החי, so it is not treated as food and cannot become impure as food.

keyTerms.meaning: Food; only something that counts as food can receive טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִין
It is not called food, meaning it does not have the legal status of food
The impurity that food can receive

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a sentence that started before this section: 'Food that you cannot feed to others is not called food.'

phrases.english: to others – is not called food.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַאֲחֵרִים – אֵין קָרוּי אוֹכֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun before this section, to the question of what רבי שמעון's reason is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food that is forbidden to everyone, so it cannot be given to others either, does not have the status of אוכל.

steps.title: Maybe the reason is that the piece is still attached
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests a different reason for רבי שמעון: since the limb or flesh is still connected to the animal, it is treated as attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Maybe רבי שמעון's reason there is that since it is attached, it counts as attached.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the reason that רבי אסי reported. He suggests that רבי שמעון might mean something else: the dangling piece is still connected to the animal, so it is treated as part of the living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון's reason is simply that the piece is attached, then רבי יוחנן's reason ('not called food') is not needed. This questions whether רבי יוחנן correctly understood רבי שמעון. This reason fits the last case of the משנה, where the animal died and the limb is still hanging from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe; introduces another possible explanation
The reason
Since, because
Attached, still connected

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
Perhaps the reason of Rabbi Shimon there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the last case of the משנה, where the animal died and רבי שמעון rules the hanging piece טהור.

phrases.english: is: since it is attached, it is considered attached.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי: דִּילְמָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason just given in step 1 by offering a different reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation (reported by רבי אסי) that רבי שמעון's reason is 'food forbidden to others is not called food'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler reason is available: the piece is still physically connected to the animal, so it is treated as part of it. That makes רבי יוחנן's reason unnecessary.

steps.title: Support from the case of the split fig branch
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא backs up his suggestion with a ברייתא about a fig branch that split off but stays connected by its bark, where רבי אסי himself gave the reason 'since it is attached, it is attached'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: a fig branch that split off but is still attached by the bark: רבי יהודה says it is pure, and the חכמים say: if it can live, it is pure, and if not, it is impure. And we asked you: what is רבי יהודה's reason? And you told us: since it is attached, it counts as attached.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a source to support his challenge. In the fig branch case, רבי אסי himself explained רבי יהודה's view with the same reason, 'it is attached', so why not use it for רבי שמעון too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit still growing on a tree cannot become impure, but picked fruit can. רבי יהודה treats a branch hanging by its bark as still attached, even if it cannot survive. The case is very similar to a hanging limb, and רבי אסי had already used this reasoning there, so רבי זירא is using רבי אסי's own words against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A branch, a shoot of a tree
Split off, broke away
Bark
Rules it pure, unable to become impure
Impure, or able to become impure

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'attached is attached' is a real halachic idea already in use, and that רבי אסי himself relied on it. That makes רבי זירא's challenge strong.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a branch of a fig tree
that split off and is still attached by the bark –
Rabbi Yehuda rules it pure,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת – טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: if it can live, it is pure,
and if not, it is impure.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִינַן לָךְ: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: And we said to you: what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: 'You' is רבי אסי. רבי זירא is reminding him of an earlier conversation.

phrases.english: And you said to us: since it is attached, it is considered attached.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יִחוּר שֶׁל תְּאֵנָה שֶׁנִּפְשַׁח וּמְעוֹרֶה בַּקְּלִיפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and precedent for רבי זירא's suggested reason in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That 'since it is attached, it is attached' could be רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a split fig branch, together with רבי אסי's own earlier explanation of רבי יהודה's view there.

steps.title: The reason refers to the middle case of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers that רבי יוחנן's reason was said about the middle case of the משנה: after the animal is slaughtered, רבי מאיר says its blood makes the hanging pieces ready to become impure, and רבי שמעון says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: [It was said] on the middle case: If the animal was slaughtered, [the limb and flesh] were made ready for impurity by its blood. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says: they were not made ready.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא. רבי יוחנן's reason was not about the last case of the משנה, where the animal died and 'it is attached' could explain רבי שמעון. It was about the middle case, where the animal has been slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the answer is placed on the middle case, רבי זירא's reason ('attached is attached') is no longer what is being explained. In that case רבי שמעון says the slaughter blood does not give the hanging pieces הכשר, and רבי יוחנן explains this by saying they are not considered food at all.

keyTerms.meaning: On the middle one; the middle case of the משנה
Was slaughtered
Was made ready (by liquid) to be able to become impure
Food becoming ready to receive impurity through contact with certain liquids, such as blood

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא suggested 'it is attached' as רבי שמעון's reason in the last case of the משנה, where the animal died. רבי אסי answered that רבי יוחנן's reason ('not called food') explains רבי שמעון in the middle case, where the animal was slaughtered and he says the blood does not make the pieces ready for impurity.
steps.confusionAlert: The animal משנה has three cases: the living animal (first), the slaughtered animal (middle), and the animal that died (last). רבי שמעון disagrees only in the middle and last cases. רבי זירא and רבי אסי are arguing about which of those two cases רבי יוחנן's reason belongs to.

phrases.english: He said to him: on the middle one:
phrases.notes: רבי אסי is answering. He means רבי יוחנן said this about the middle case of the משנה.

phrases.english: If the animal was slaughtered, it was made ready by its blood –
phrases.notes: The blood from the slaughter counts as a liquid that makes the hanging pieces ready for impurity.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir;
Rabbi Shimon says: they were not made ready.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אַמְּצִיעֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 2 and 3 by moving רבי יוחנן's reason to a different case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocation: the explanation is applied to a different clause of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא assumed רבי יוחנן was explaining רבי שמעון in the last case (an animal that died), where 'it is attached' would be enough of a reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was explaining רבי שמעון in the middle case (a slaughtered animal), where רבי שמעון says the blood does not give הכשר, because the hanging pieces are not considered food.

steps.title: The verse-based reason is now placed on the middle case
steps.stepSummary: As part of רבי אסי's answer, the גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's reason for רבי שמעון. The reason comes from the פסוק 'from all food which may be eaten': only food you can give to others counts as food. This time the reason is attached to the middle case of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said that רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says 'from all food which may be eaten.' Food you are able to feed to others is called food. Food you are not able to feed to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's reason word for word. Now it is attached to the middle case of the משנה, the case after the animal was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as before, but the job is new. רבי אסי is using this reason to explain why רבי שמעון says the slaughter blood does not make the hanging pieces ready for impurity. Those pieces are forbidden to everyone, so they are not 'food' that anyone could be fed.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason behind a ruling
A פסוק (verse) from the תורה
Food, meaning something that can become impure the way food does
To feed it to others, including non-Jews

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new teaching. It is the same reason from the start of this discussion, repeated here because רבי אסי now applies it to the middle case.

phrases.english: (Rabbi Asi said that) Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. Either way, רבי אסי is the one quoting רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
The verse says: 'From all food which may be eaten'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים – קָרוּי אוֹכֶל,
phrases.english: Food that you are able to feed to others is called food.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים – אֵין קָרוּי אוֹכֶל.
phrases.english: Food that you are not able to feed to others is not called food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אסי's answer from step 4 by restating the reason that now applies to the middle case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the reason to a different case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason was thought to be about the last case, where רבי זירא suggested a simpler reason: the piece is still attached.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason is about the middle case, where the slaughter blood touches the animal.

steps.title: The middle case already has other explanations
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges again. In the middle case, רבי שמעון's view has already been explained another way, either like רבא or like רבי יוחנן's own earlier explanation. So there is no need for the 'not food' reason there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe רבי שמעון's reason in that case is either like רבא's explanation or like רבי יוחנן's explanation?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא objects to placing the 'not food' reason on the middle case. רבי שמעון's ruling there already has other known reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק, רבא and רבי יוחנן each gave a reason for רבי שמעון in the middle case. Neither reason has anything to do with 'food you cannot give others.' If those reasons already explain the middle case, רבי יוחנן's verse-based reason is not needed there.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; it opens a different possibility that weakens the last claim
In that one, meaning the middle case
Either... or...

phrases.english: But perhaps the reason of Rabbi Shimon in that case
is either like Rava or like Rabbi Yoḥanan?
phrases.notes: These are the two explanations given earlier in the פרק for רבי שמעון in the middle case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּהָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from steps 4-5 that placed the 'not food' reason on the middle case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's claim that רבי יוחנן's verse-based reason is about the middle case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle case is already explained by רבא's reason or by רבי יוחנן's earlier reason, so the 'not food' reason is not needed there.

steps.title: Back to the last case, but about the flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's reason really does belong to the last case, where the animal died. However, רבי שמעון's ruling there is applied to the hanging flesh, not the hanging limb. רבי מאיר says the flesh needs הכשר, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really refers to the last case. It is not about the limb, but about the flesh. The animal died: the flesh needs הכשר, and רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the middle case and returns to the last case of the משנה. It changes which item רבי שמעון is talking about: the flesh instead of the limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linking רבי שמעון to the flesh lets the 'food you cannot give others' reason fit again. The hanging flesh is forbidden to everyone, so to רבי שמעון it is not 'food' and cannot become impure as food. That is why he says it stays טהור even after touching liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, actually; it returns to an earlier approach
The last case of the משנה
A limb
Flesh or meat
Being made ready to become impure by touching liquid
Rules it טהור (pure)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי יוחנן's reason ('food you cannot give others is not food') explains רבי שמעון in the last case, about the hanging flesh of an animal that died.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא working to find the one spot in the משנה where this verse-based reason is truly needed and where no other explanation already covers the case.

phrases.english: Rather, actually, it refers to the last case,
and not to the limb, but to the flesh.
If the animal died, the flesh needs to be made ready for impurity,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's view in the last case of the משנה.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon rules it pure.
phrases.notes: Read this now as talking about the hanging flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 by leaving the middle case and going back to the last case, now applied to the flesh.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which item in the case the ruling refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's ruling in the last case was about the limb, where the reason 'it is still attached' could explain it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון's ruling is about the hanging flesh of a dead animal, explained by 'food you cannot give others is not food.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason is restated for the hanging flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's reason for רבי שמעון, now applied to the hanging flesh when the animal died: food that cannot be given to others is not called food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says 'from all food which may be eaten.' Food you can feed to others is called food. Food you cannot feed to others is not called food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 7 by quoting רבי יוחנן's reason one more time. This time the reason is aimed at the hanging flesh of the animal that died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flesh hanging from an animal is treated like flesh from a living animal, and nobody, not even a non-Jew, may eat that. So it is food you cannot give to others. Because of that, רבי שמעון says it is not 'food' for טומאה at all, and so it is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
To feed it to others
Is called food (counts as food for טומאה)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי יוחנן's 'not food' reason belongs to the last case, where the animal died. It explains why רבי שמעון calls the hanging flesh טהור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
The verse says
"From all food which may be eaten"
Food that you are able to feed to others
is called food.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹכֶל שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַאֲכִילוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים
phrases.english: Food that you are not able to feed to others
is not called food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 7's answer by quoting רבי יוחנן's reason, now attached to the hanging flesh in the last case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the reason to a different part of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason seemed to have no place, because the middle case was already explained in other ways.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason explains רבי שמעון's ruling that the hanging flesh is טהור in the case where the animal died.

steps.title: New משנה: a limb or flesh hanging from a person
steps.stepSummary: A limb or flesh hanging from a living person is טהור. After the person dies, רבי מאיר says the flesh is טהור and the limb carries טומאה as a limb from the living, not as a limb from the dead. רבי שמעון says it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb or flesh hanging from a person is pure. If the person died, the flesh is pure. The limb makes things impure as a limb from a living person, but not as a limb from a dead person. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from animals to a person, and asks what happens to a limb or flesh that is hanging from someone's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the person is alive, the hanging parts are still attached, so they are טהור. Once he dies, רבי מאיר looks at the hanging limb as if it fell off while he was still alive, so it carries the טומאה of אבר מן החי. רבי שמעון disagrees and rules it טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Hanging, partly cut off but still attached
A limb cut off from a living person, which carries טומאה
A limb from a dead body
Declares it pure

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about a person, not an animal. Here the question is whether the limb carries the טומאה of a body part, not whether it counts as food.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The limb and the flesh that are hanging from a person
are pure.
If the person died,
the flesh is pure.

phrases.aramaic: הָאֵבֶר מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי,
phrases.english: The limb makes impure as a limb from the living,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת,
phrases.english: and does not make impure as a limb from the dead;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And Rabbi Shimon declares it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאֵבֶר וְהַבָּשָׂר הַמְדוּלְדָּלִין בְּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The topic moves from hanging parts of an animal to hanging parts of a person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hanging limb or flesh is טהור while the person lives. After death, רבי מאיר says the flesh is טהור and the limb carries the טומאה of אבר מן החי. רבי שמעון says it is טהור.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's view seems impossible either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's ruling. If death makes the limb count as fallen off, it should carry the טומאה of a limb from the living. If not, it should carry the טומאה of a limb from the dead. Either way, it should not be טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, whichever way you look at it, is hard to understand. If death makes the limb count as fallen off, it should make impure as a limb from the living. If death does not make it fallen off, it should make impure as a limb from the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון with a 'whichever way you look at it' argument. It shows that both possible ways of seeing the limb lead to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two options. Either the limb is seen as having fallen off before death, so it is אבר מן החי, or it is seen as still attached at death, so it is part of the dead body. Both options make it טמא, so how can רבי שמעון call it טהור?

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (both options cause a problem)
Death makes the hanging limb count as if it fell off
It should make impure

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And Rabbi Shimon, whichever way you look at it, what is he thinking?
If death makes it count as fallen off,
let it make impure as a limb from the living;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מָה נַפְשָׁךְ

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that the hanging limb is טהור after the person dies
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible ways of seeing the limb, fallen off before death or attached at death, lead to טומאה. So 'טהור' seems impossible.

steps.title: רבי שמעון is arguing about a limb from the dead in general
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון is not ruling on the hanging limb itself. רבי מאיר's words imply that a limb from a dead body is generally טמא, and רבי שמעון answers that in general it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון is talking about the general case. The תנא קמא said the limb makes impure as a limb from the living and not as a limb from the dead. That shows he holds that a limb from a dead person in general makes impure. רבי שמעון said to him: a limb from a dead person, in general, does not make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that רבי שמעון's word 'טהור' is aimed at a general idea in רבי מאיר's words, not at this specific limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said the limb 'does not make impure as a limb from the dead.' That suggests a normal limb from a dead body would make things impure. רבי שמעון disagrees with that general point, so his ruling does not contradict the 'whichever way' argument about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: He is talking about the general case
The first opinion in the משנה (here, רבי מאיר)
Evidently, this shows that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי שמעון as saying this hanging limb is pure. He is arguing with a side point that comes out of רבי מאיר's words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon is referring to the general case,
since the first tanna said:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּעָלְמָא קָאֵי

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the statement to a general idea, not the specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון was ruling that this hanging limb is טהור, which seemed impossible either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון is rejecting the general idea, implied by רבי מאיר, that a limb from a dead body makes things impure.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's tradition: a limb from the living is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says he heard that a limb from the living makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי אליעזר said, 'I heard that a limb from a living person makes things impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier source showing that the argument from step 11 also appears among older תנאים. It starts with רבי אליעזר's tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר mentions only a limb from the living. That suggests a limb from the dead is not טמא, which fits רבי שמעון's view from step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb, a body part with flesh, sinews and bone
From the living, cut off from someone still alive
Makes things impure, passes on טומאה

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer said:
I heard that a limb from the living imparts impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁאֵבֶר מִן הַחַי מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier source that parallels the argument in step 11 about whether a limb from a dead body is טמא.
steps.raayaObject: The view, like רבי שמעון's, that a limb from the dead is not טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר's received tradition

steps.title: רבי יהושע's קל וחומר: a limb from the dead should be impure too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר. If a limb from a pure living person is טמא, then a limb from a dead body, which is itself טמא, should certainly be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: 'Only from the living and not from the dead? There is a קל וחומר. A living person is pure, and still a limb that comes off him is impure. A dead body is impure, so isn't it all the more so that its limb is impure?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks the idea that only a limb from the living is טמא. He uses a קל וחומר, which is reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The light case is a living person, who is טהור, yet his limb is טמא. The strong case is a dead body, which is already טמא, so its limb should surely be טמא. This matches רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger case
If, in a case where... (the opening of a קל וחומר)
All the more so
Pure
Impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
From the living, and not from the dead?
But it is a kal vachomer:
If a living person, who is pure,
a limb that separates from him is impure;

phrases.aramaic: מֵת שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא, לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: a corpse, which is impure, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הַחַי וְלֹא מִן הַמֵּת? וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only a limb from the living is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a limb from a pure living person is טמא, a limb from an already impure dead body must be טמא too.

steps.title: A comparison from מגילת תענית: mentioning the smaller case includes the bigger one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע shows that when a rule is stated about a smaller case, it does not exclude the bigger case. It applies there all the more so.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written in מגילת תענית: 'On the small פסח one does not eulogize.' Does that mean on the big פסח one may eulogize?! No. It means all the more so. Here too, a limb from the living is mentioned, and a limb from the dead is included all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע backs up his קל וחומר with an example. A text that mentions only the smaller case can still mean the bigger case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's tradition said 'from the living', which could sound like it leaves out the dead. רבי יהושע shows from מגילת תענית that naming the smaller case does not leave out the bigger one. It includes it all the more so.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancient list of days on which fasting and eulogies are not allowed
The small פסח, the 14th of אייר
To eulogize, to make a הספד
All the more so (Aramaic)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches an important way of reading: naming a smaller case does not always leave out a bigger case.

phrases.english: It is written in Megillat Ta'anit:
"On the minor Passover one does not eulogize"
phrases.notes: The small פסח is the 14th of אייר, and the big פסח is the 14th of ניסן.

phrases.english: Does that mean that on the major one one may eulogize?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהושע's challenge from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Mentioning only a limb from the living does not leave out a limb from the dead
steps.raayaSupportSource: מגילת תענית about the small פסח and the big פסח

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reply: this is what I received
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does not argue with the logic. He simply says that this is the tradition he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'This is what I heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע by holding on to his tradition. He says, 'This is what I heard.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not offer a counter-argument. A received tradition stands even against a strong קל וחומר, so the argument stays open. That is why it can line up with the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I heard, a received tradition
I heard
So, in this way

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds, by tradition, that only a limb from the living is טמא, like רבי שמעון. רבי יהושע holds, by קל וחומר, that a limb from the dead is טמא too, like רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: He said to him: Thus I heard.

steps.terutzMaskana: A received tradition is not overturned by the קל וחומר, so רבי אליעזר keeps his view.

steps.title: What difference does it make which kind of limb it counts as?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between טומאה of a limb from the living and a limb from the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference is there between a limb from the living and a limb from the dead?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי מאיר's words in step 9. He said the hanging limb is טמא 'as a limb from the living, not as a limb from the dead.' The גמרא asks what that changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of limb are טמא, so it seems not to matter which name we give it. The גמרא wants to know the practical result.

steps.title: The difference: small pieces that come off the limb
steps.stepSummary: The difference is about an olive-size of flesh or a barley-size bone that separates from the limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is an olive-size of flesh or a barley-size bone that separates from a limb from the living.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The difference shows up with small pieces that fall off the limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A piece that size from a dead body is clearly טמא. If the limb counts as a limb from the living, then according to some opinions those small pieces are טהור. So calling it a limb from the living changes the דין of its pieces.

A bone

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is the דין of an olive-size of flesh or a barley-size bone that separates from the limb.

steps.title: The משנה showing the argument about those small pieces
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that the תנאים argue about an olive-size of flesh and a barley-size bone that come off a limb from the living.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: an olive-size of flesh that separates from a limb from the living, רבי אליעזר says it is impure, and רבי נחוניא בן הקנה and רבי יהושע say it is pure. A barley-size bone that separates from a limb from the living, רבי נחוניא says it is impure, and רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע say it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that the small pieces from a limb from the living have a different דין. Some תנאים say those pieces are pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For flesh, רבי אליעזר says it is טמא, while רבי נחוניא and רבי יהושע say it is טהור. For bone, רבי נחוניא says it is טמא, while רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע say it is טהור. Pieces from a dead body would be טמא no matter what, so here we see the real difference between the two kinds of limb.

keyTerms.meaning: They rule it pure
Flesh
From a limb

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. רבי אליעזר says the flesh is טמא but the bone is טהור. רבי נחוניא says the bone is טמא but the flesh is טהור. רבי יהושע says both are טהור.
steps.whatToRemember: When רבי מאיר says the limb is טמא 'as a limb from the living', its small pieces follow the more lenient דין of a limb from the living, not the דין of pieces from a dead body.

steps.title: The same difference explains תנא קמא and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know תנאים argue about a separated כזית of flesh and כשעורה of bone, the difference between תנא קמא and רבי שמעון in the משנה can also be this same case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, between the first תנא and רבי שמעון too, the difference between them is an olive-size of flesh and a barley-size bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the argument it just found and uses it to explain another argument in our משנה. The argument between תנא קמא and רבי שמעון is also about a separated piece of flesh or bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we might have thought there was no real difference between תנא קמא and רבי שמעון. But since we now know that תנאים argue about flesh and bone that come off a limb from the living, we can say תנא קמא follows one side and רבי שמעון follows another side. So the practical difference is about the same small pieces: a כזית of flesh and a כשעורה of bone.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this: now that we have reached this idea, we can use it here too

An olive-size piece of flesh

steps.whatToRemember: One argument among the תנאים, about a separated כזית of flesh and כשעורה of bone, explains two places: the difference between טומאה of a limb from the living and from the dead, and the argument between תנא קמא and רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא reuses one answer to solve another open question. Once a real practical difference is found, it can explain more than one argument in the משנה.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical difference between תנא קמא and רבי שמעון is also a separated כזית of flesh or כשעורה of bone. Each side follows a different view in the argument about a limb from the living.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing הָעוֹר וְהָרוֹטֶב
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter הָעוֹר וְהָרוֹטֶב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הָעוֹר וְהָרוֹטֶב.

steps.deeperAnalysis: With this line the פרק הָעוֹר וְהָרוֹטֶב is finished. The words express a promise to come back and learn this chapter again.
